ig_carousel_topic.topic: Hedging, when it's smart, when it's just buying back losses
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Should you hedge that ticket?
Sometimes yes. Usually no. The difference matters more than you think.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors hedge because they're scared, not because the math says to. That's not strategy. That's emotion with extra steps.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Hedging makes sense when your original bet has moved significantly in your favor and you can lock in a profit across both outcomes. The key word: profit. Not 'reduce the loss.' Actual guaranteed profit on both sides.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: You bet Team A ML at +200. They won their first three games. Now they're -140 favorites in the final. A hedge on the other side at +120 can guarantee you green regardless of outcome. That's a real hedge.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Buying back a losing position just to 'get something back' is not hedging. It's doubling your exposure to a bad bet. Hedge only when both legs of the math work in your favor.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Hedging isn't always smart. Sometimes it's just panic with a second receipt. Know the difference before you place that second bet.
